welcome.title: Swipe less. Feel well.
welcome.body: Thumbwell counts the Reels, Shorts and TikToks you watch and pauses them when you reach your daily limit. No account needed.
welcome.testBody: Counting works on Instagram, YouTube and TikTok. Thanks for helping us test!

disclosure.title: Thumbwell uses Accessibility to count your reels.
disclosure.pointLock: Shows the lock screen when you hit your limit
disclosure.pointPrivacy: Never reads your messages, never sends screen content anywhere
disclosure.p1: To count Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and TikTok videos, Thumbwell uses Android's AccessibilityService API. Only while one of these apps is open, it reads the structure of the screen on your phone — which screen is showing, the labels of on-screen elements, and scroll events — to tell when a new short video starts.
disclosure.p2: We use this only to count the short videos you watch and show you your count. While one of these apps is open, Thumbwell also shows a small movable counter on top of it, so you can see your count as you scroll; you can turn it off in Thumbwell settings. When you reach your limit, Thumbwell covers the reels screen with a break screen, using Android's separate "Display over other apps" permission, which you can turn off at any time in Android Settings. Thumbwell may also pause the video that is playing at that moment, by tapping the screen or the video's pause button for you. Tapping "Leave reels" takes you to the app's Home tab.
disclosure.p3: Everything is processed on your phone. Thumbwell does not store any text it sees, does not record your screen, and does not keep or send your messages, comments or anything about the videos. Your counts stay on your phone.
disclosure.p4: You can turn this off at any time in Android Settings → Accessibility.
disclosure.check: I understand and agree that Thumbwell uses the Accessibility service as described above.
disclosure.disclaimer: Not affiliated with or endorsed by Meta, Google/YouTube, TikTok or Snap Inc. All trademarks belong to their owners. Not a medical device.

guide.title: Turn on Thumbwell in Accessibility
guide.path: Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Thumbwell → ON
guide.headsUp: Android shows a strong warning for every Accessibility app. That is normal. Thumbwell only does what the previous screen lists.
guide.helpBody: Open Accessibility settings, choose Installed apps (on some phones Downloaded apps), tap Thumbwell and switch it on. Then come back here.
guide.stillOffBody: Thumbwell is not switched on yet. Open Accessibility settings and turn it on.
guide.restrictedBody: Android 13 and newer blocks Accessibility for apps installed outside Google Play. Open App info, tap the three dots at the top right, choose Allow restricted settings, then turn Thumbwell on.
guide.successBody: Counting starts now. Reels, Shorts and TikToks you watch will show up on Home.
guide.panelHint: Example of the Android Accessibility screen. Your phone may look a little different.

ask.title: Let Thumbwell show over other apps
ask.intro: Android calls this “Display over other apps”. It is one switch, and you can turn it off any time.
ask.does1: Covers the video when you reach your limit
ask.does2: Shows your count badge on top of reels
ask.never1: Never reads what is on your screen
ask.previewTitle: What you will see in Android
ask.previewHint: Turn it on, then press Back to return here.
ask.skipNote: You can skip this step. Thumbwell then uses the fallback overlay: it still covers reels at your limit, but leaves a strip at the top of the screen free. Turn it on any time in Settings.

granted.title: You’re all set
granted.body: At your limit, Thumbwell covers the video and offers one button: Leave reels. It never reads what is on your screen.
granted.cardBody: Open Thumbwell Settings, tap Display over other apps, then switch Thumbwell off in Android. The lock then uses the fallback overlay.

off.chip: Display over other apps: Not enabled
off.title: No problem. The lock still works
off.body: The lock will use the fallback overlay. It still covers reels at your limit, but leaves a strip at the top of the screen free.
off.cardBody: Thumbwell Settings → Display over other apps. It shows “Not enabled” until you turn it on.

settings.offHint: To switch it off, find Thumbwell in the list and turn the switch off.
